newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia party concerned as poll result announced.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia party concerned as poll result announced.

text.p: Indonesia's three authorised political parties on Monday formally accepted the results of May 29 general elections, but one party expressed concern about alleged poll violations and the conduct of the campaign.

The General Election Institute (LPU) announced in a detailed briefing witnessed by ministers, military figures and the nation's 27 governors that the ruling Golkar party had won 325 seats in the 500-member national parliament.

It said the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) won 89 seats, while the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) received 11 seats. The military, who do not vote, automatically receive 75 seats.
PPP chairman Ismail Hasan Metareum told the LPU ceremony that his party would accept the result in the interests of the nation, but added:

"The PPP notes the increase in violations and fraud during the implementation of the 1997 general election which were done by many of the implementing officials, so that in general the quality of the 1997 election was not better than the preceding elections.
"The PPP is increasingly certain there needs to be changes to general election laws in order that the implementation of the next election will be more democratic, fair, honest and just," he said.

Golkar chairman Harmoko replied that his party considered the election to be of high quality despite being regarded by many analysts as the most violent campaign ever and widespread allegations of poll irregularities.
"From Sabang (in Aceh in the west) to Merauke (in Irian Jaya in the east) the election for the most part was orderly and safe," Harmoko told the ceremony.
"There were some disturbances but these were only small and we regard them not as political but purely criminal actions which must be dealt with by the law," he said.
The LPU's figures showed Golkar received 84,187,907 votes, ahead of the PPP's 25,340,028 and the PDI's 3,463,225.

Interior Minister Yogie Memet, who heads the LPU, said 112,161,955 valid votes had been cast from the 124,740,987 registered voters in the nation of more than 200 million people, with voter turnout reaching 93.38 percent.
He said the number of spoiled ballots was 4.2 percent, the same as in the 1992 poll.
On preliminary results, the PDI had been tipped to only receive 10 seats, below the minimum of 11 required by the legislature's rules.
PDI Secretary-General Buttu Hutapea denied his party had received any votes from other contestants, particularly in North Sumatra province where it won two seats.
The PPP had alleged that its figures showed the PDI was more than 60,000 votes short of winning two seats in that province.

A dozen youths with placards alleging vote manipulation in favour of the PDI in North Sumatra briefly protested outside the LPU after the results were announced, shouting slogans in support of the PPP and ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
"We did not ask for any votes and up to now we have not had anyone give us any votes," Hutapea told the ceremony.
The PDI was badly split after former party chief Megawati was ousted from her post last year at a government-backed congress in Medan in North Sumatra.
She had told supporters not to campaign for the PDI or vote for the party under the leadership of her rival Surjadi.
